script: If your dog shoves their way between you and another dog getting attention, that's not a coincidence, and researchers have actually studied this. In one well known experiment, dogs were far more likely to push, nudge, or physically interrupt their owner when the owner petted a realistic stuffed dog compared to when the owner interacted with a non-dog object. That points to something real happening emotionally, at least a basic form of jealousy tied to protecting a valued relationship. Scientists debate whether dogs experience jealousy exactly the way humans do, with all the complex social comparison involved, or whether it's a simpler response rooted in resource guarding, treating your attention like a limited resource worth competing for. Either way, the behavior is consistent, dogs act differently when they sense their bond with you is being challenged. This is actually useful information for multi-dog households. Giving each dog individual attention, not just group affection, can prevent a lot of tension and competitive behavior before it starts. So yes, that judgmental stare when you're cuddling another dog is very real, and very deliberate. If you want practical tools for managing dynamics like this, check the link below.
